Why durable steps matter

A background job that dies halfway through usually starts again from scratch. If the first half called a paid API, you pay for it twice. Durable execution fixes this by recording the result of every step the moment it succeeds.

When the process comes back, the engine replays the function from the top, but every step that already finished returns its recorded result instantly instead of running again. Only the step that failed, and the ones after it, do real work.

This turns retries from a liability into something you can lean on. You can crash a worker on purpose in the middle of an expensive embedding call and watch it pick up exactly there.
